claim: On the char_ngram task (language domain, 3-character context, 27-way next-character prediction), the pinned arm digital/feedforward/instantaneous/null/gradient/adam reaches a validation perplexity of at most 5.0 at the L2 schedule (5 seeds x 20 epochs) — at least 4.75x below the 23.77 unigram ruler measured on the same 1,024-item validation split.

ruler.name: unigram perplexity over the validation split's target characters
ruler.split: char_ngram validation split (seed=1, 1,024 items, 24 distinct target classes)
ruler.note: Computed from the split the cell measures: counts over the 1,024 validation targets, renormalized over the observed classes. B4 quoted 25.21 from a different estimator; the smaller ruler is the harder one to beat and is the one registered here.

secondary_metric.note: Reported beside the primary metric; not part of the decision rule.

decision_rule: Met iff (1) every one of the 5 seeds writes PASS with val_ppl <= 5.0, and (2) the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound of the seed mean (t, df=4) is < 5.0. Marginal iff the seed mean is within 1 SE of 5.0. Distance from the threshold is reported in SEs of the seed mean and as a perplexity ratio against the ruler.
pilot_role: Schedule choice, not threshold choice: TODO90 B4 measured 3.9923 at 10 epochs / 1 seed, and a 20-epoch / 1-seed pilot this session measured 2.5869. The 20-epoch schedule is registered because it is the ladder's L2 default; the 5.0 threshold is derived from the ruler (a 4.75x reduction), not from either pilot number.
claim_eligibility: L2 records carry 5 achieved PASS seeds, a replay hash, and a normalized metric, so the run's claim-eligible cell count is non-zero (the B6 acceptance's 'claim' evidence).
